subject: Vendor showdown summary + prioritized experiments and owners
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@orchardai.com>, Michael Soto <mike@orchardai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor showdown summary + prioritized experiments and owners

Hi Elaine / Michael — thanks again for the demo and the candid discussion earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of experiments so we can accelerate your decision process this week. I called out owners and rough timeline so we can close the loop quickly.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Token-level cost at scale: production prompts today are expensive; target is ~50% unit-cost drop vs your current endpoint.
- Tail latency for short queries (95th/99th) is causing poor UX for agent-triggered flows.
- Data governance: you need per-tenant isolation and audit logs for compliance.

Stated goals / decision criteria (aligned to what you said):
1) Cost per 1k tokens (primary)
2) 95th percentile latency under 300ms for <256-token responses (secondary)
3) SOC2 readiness + egress controls (required)
4) Smooth rollout path: canary + fallback to cheaper variant (nice to have)

Proposed prioritized experiments (owners & ETA):
A. Short-run latency probe — run 10k synthetic short queries against our low-latency variant, measure p95/p99. Owner: Camila. ETA: 48 hours.
B. Cost model trial — replay 1M tokens of your anonymized sample traffic through our optimizer to estimate token/unit cost with batching + prefix caching. Owner: Karthik. ETA: 4 business days.
C. Isolation & logging proof — provide an audit log extract and KMS key test for your compliance team. Owner: Marissa. ETA: 3 business days.
D. Head-to-head QA tests — 10 representative prompts across three competitor endpoints (you provided) + Redwood; results table with failure modes. Owner: Camila + Orchard QA. ETA: 5 business days.

Attachments: redwood-vs-competitors-matrix.xlsx (matrix with proposed metrics), poa-test-scenarios.md (detailed probe specs). Links to the Drive folder are below.

Asks from you to unblock:
- Please confirm which of the three competitors you want in the head-to-head (default: Competitor A, Competitor C, and their internal endpoint).
- Can you share a 48-hour anonymized sample of production traffic (S3 link or Drive) and confirm PII scrubbed?
- Who should our SOC2 contact coordinate with at Orchard for a short evidence exchange?

If you’re aligned I’ll kick off A and D immediately and loop Karthik / Marissa where needed.

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor showdown summary + prioritized experiments and owners

Thanks Camila — this is super helpful and aligns with our internal notes. Quick answers while we loop the security folks: 

- Competitor set: please include Competitor A and Competitor B (we realized Competitor C is not in our shortlist anymore).
- Sample data: I can share an anonymized S3 snapshot (logs + prompts) by EOD Monday. Will scrub obvious PII but will confirm with our data team — if Redwood needs a signed NDA for the sample exchange, let me know.
- SOC2 contact: forwarding to our security lead, Mike Soto, on this thread.

Priority adjustments from our side (we want to be explicit):
1) Cost estimate and predictable unit economics (top priority)
2) Reliability for peak traffic (we run bursts during nightly jobs)
3) Compliance evidence (must satisfy internal auditors)

Open questions for Redwood — can you call out whether the latency probe will be run on our real payload or synthetic traffic? Also, do you support per-tenant KMS key rotation on Dedicated?

We can do a 30-min checkpoint Tue morning (9/21) to review initial numbers if that works for you.

Best,
Elaine

Thanks for the clarifications, Elaine — we'll proceed with Competitor A + Competitor B. A few specifics in response to your questions: 

- Latency probe: we'll run the short-run latency probe (A) with synthetic traffic that mirrors your production token-length distribution for the first pass (to avoid PII handling delays). If the initial p95 looks good you can green-light an instrumented run on your anonymized sample (we'll only need a signed DPA/NDA if your legal requires it).
- Per-tenant KMS rotation: yes on Dedicated — we integrate with customer-managed KMS and support rotation policies; Marissa will coordinate the evidence exchange.

Action plan (confirmed):
- Camila: kick off latency probe (synthetic) today and share results by end-of-day Sat.
- Karthik: run cost-model replay once we receive the anonymized sample; target report Thu.
- Marissa: prepare SOC2 evidence checklist and a short workflow for key rotation; target Wed.

Can we lock Tue 9/21 at 09:00 PT for a 30-minute checkpoint? I'll send a calendar invite after this note.

Attachments: none in this message (matrix and scenarios already attached in initial). Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEfGhIj

Thanks — Camila
